t: Isfahan was a regional centre under the Medes and a city of mixed peoples under the Achaemenids, and it grew under the Buyids and the Seljuks, whose ruler Toghril Beg made it his capital in the mid-11th century.

Timur's army killed, reportedly, 70,000 of its people in 1387, but in 1598 Abbas the Great made it the Safavid capital and rebuilt it round a new square and a boulevard, settling craftsmen and Armenians there by force.
After Central Asian invaders sacked it in 1722 it declined, and the capital moved to Mashhad, then to Shiraz, and in 1775 to Tehran.
dyk: Timur's soldiers reportedly killed 70,000 people in Isfahan in 1387, and an eyewitness counted more than 28 towers, each built of about 1,500 heads.
ev: Cyrus the Great issues the edict allowing Jews in Babylon to return to Jerusalem, and some settle in Isfahan instead
Muslim Arabs capture Isfahan and make it the capital of al-Jibal province
Toghril Beg makes Isfahan the capital of the Seljuk domains
Timur's soldiers massacre the people of Isfahan after a revolt against his taxes
Abbas the Great moves his capital from Qazvin to Isfahan
Abbas II builds the Khaju Bridge
Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar moves the capital to Tehran

f.founded: No founding date is known: the area was inhabited from the Palaeolithic, the site became a regional centre under the Medes, and a diverse city is recorded under Cyrus the Great, whose edict of 538 BCE is the first date connected with it.
f.where: On the plain of the Zayandeh River at the foot of the Zagros Mountains, 440 kilometres south of Tehran, in Isfahan Province, Iran.
f.known: The Seljuk capital under Malik-Shah I; Timur's massacre of 1387; Abbas the Great's capital from 1598; Naqsh-e Jahan Square and the Chahar Bagh boulevard; the bridges over the Zayandeh; New Julfa and its Armenians; the proverb 'Isfahan is half the world'
f.today: Isfahan is the capital of Isfahan Province and the third most populous city in Iran, with a population of about 2,238,000.
